drafts.title: Give customers direct control to view, export and permanently delete their driver profile and data sharing settings
drafts.description: Customers can inspect what personal data is stored in their driver profile, export a complete copy, permanently delete their profile and toggle explicit opt-in for data sharing from the vehicle or companion app.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Users can (a) export a complete driver-profile data package (JSON or ZIP) from the vehicle or app within 60 seconds and receive a downloadable file, (b) permanently delete their driver profile and receive a confirmation that deletion requests have been queued within 60 seconds and completed within 24 hours, and (c) enable/disable all non-essential data sharing with a single on/off control; tests show the export and delete flows succeed in 95% of attempts in lab verification.
assumptions: Backend services can correlate and delete profile data across vehicle and cloud services within 24 hours when the user requests deletion.
Export formats (JSON/ZIP) are acceptable to customers and supported by downstream BMW cloud exports.
Some legally required records (for warranty, safety or tax) may remain in separate audit logs; deletion scope is limited to the user-facing driver profile and associated personal data.
uncertainties: Exact backend propagation time for all connected services may vary by region and integration partners.

drafts.title: Improve voice control so common driving commands are recognized reliably while driving
drafts.description: Voice assistant understands and executes simple driving-related commands reliably even with typical cabin noise and different accents, reducing driver distraction from repeating commands.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a lab usability test with typical driving noise (up to 85 dB) and five common English accents, the voice assistant correctly recognizes and executes a set of 30 common driving commands (navigation, climate, media, phone) in at least 95% of utterances.
assumptions: High-quality microphone array and noise-cancellation preprocessing are available in the vehicle's cabin audio system.
Cloud or on-board natural language understanding models can be updated to improve recognition accuracy.
uncertainties: Recognition rates may vary for uncommon accents or non-native speakers; background music and aftermarket soundproofing can change noise profile.

drafts.title: Make the wireless phone charging pad reliably keep phones charging during normal use
drafts.description: When a phone is placed correctly on the vehicle's wireless charging pad, it stays charging reliably for the duration of typical drives and across common phone models and case thicknesses.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In tests with the top 10 phone models by market share and common protective cases up to 3 mm thickness, 95% of correctly placed phones maintain continuous charging for 30-minute driving scenarios (no unintended disconnects).
assumptions: Phones use the Qi standard and are among the leading market models at launch; very thick metal cases or magnetic attachments are excluded.
The vehicle provides firmware to manage foreign object detection with sensible thresholds to avoid false disconnects.
uncertainties: Aftermarket phone attachments (metal mounts, battery packs) may still interfere and are outside guaranteed behavior.

drafts.title: Provide tactile physical controls for temperature and fan speed that can be used without looking
drafts.description: Temperature and fan speed are controllable via distinct, tactile physical controls that drivers can locate and operate by touch while driving, avoiding reliance on the touchscreen.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In usability tests, users can set a target temperature and adjust fan speed using only touch (eyes closed) within 5 seconds in at least 90% of attempts.
assumptions: There is sufficient dashboard space to implement clear tactile controls with distinct haptics.
Controls will be designed with differentiable shapes and detents to support blind operation.
uncertainties: Customers who prefer fully touch-based interiors may perceive these controls as redundant; layout choices must balance aesthetics and usability.

drafts.title: Ensure both the head-up display and center screen remain readable in bright sunlight
drafts.description: Driver-facing displays (HUD and central instrument/display) remain legible and show sufficient contrast in direct sunlight and high-reflection conditions so drivers do not have to shade the screen to read critical information.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Under a standardized bright-sun test (direct sun up to 100,000 lux and common viewing angles), both the head-up display and center screen achieve a legibility/user readability score of ≥90% in user trials and retain key information visibility (time, speed, navigation prompts, climate status).
assumptions: Hardware options like higher peak brightness, anti-reflective coatings, and adaptive brightness control are available for the successor vehicle.
HUD projection and center-display coatings and software can be tuned together to meet legibility targets.
uncertainties: Extreme sun angles combined with aftermarket windshield films may still reduce readability for some users.

drafts.title: Include the heated steering wheel within the vehicle's Cold Weather package
drafts.description: Customers who choose the Cold Weather package receive a heated steering wheel as part of that package rather than as a separate, high-cost standalone option.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At launch, the heated steering wheel is included as a standard feature on 100% of vehicles ordered with the Cold Weather package (all trims/steering-wheel variants) and is selectable only via that package in the configurator.
assumptions: Supplier capacity supports including the heated-steering-wheel hardware as part of the Cold Weather package across trims.
Configuration and ordering systems can enforce package inclusion at launch.
uncertainties: Some specialized steering-wheel trims may require alternative heating elements or slight lead times for supplier tooling.

drafts.title: Offer heated seats as a digitally activatable subscription from the in-car store and companion app
drafts.description: Customers can enable heated seats via a digital subscription product directly from the vehicle UI or the BMW app, with immediate activation and a trial option to evaluate the feature before committing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Customers can purchase or start a trial for heated-seat activation from the in-car digital store or companion app and have the feature activated in the vehicle within 2 minutes in 95% of successful activation attempts; subscription can be toggled on/off by the customer immediately with the effect applied to the vehicle within 2 minutes.
assumptions: Billing and entitlement systems are integrated with the vehicle and companion app at launch.
Heated-seat hardware is present in vehicles ordered with the subscription-capable trim (subscription controls only enable/disable existing hardware).
uncertainties: Regional app-store/billing restrictions and local payment methods may affect activation times in some markets.
